chapters.title: The Song of the Gopis — Longing for Krishna

verses.sanskrit:
जयति तेऽधिकं जन्मना व्रजः श्रयत इन्दिरा शश्वदत्र हि ।
दयित दृश्यतां दिक्षु तावकास्त्वयि धृतासवस्त्वां विचिन्वते ॥
verses.translation: O beloved, Your birth in Vraja has made it more glorious than Vaikuntha, for the goddess of fortune, Indira, always resides here. Dear Lord, please reveal Yourself to us — we who have given our life breath to You are searching for You everywhere.

verses.sanskrit:
शरदुदाशये साधुजातसत्सरसिजोदरश्रीमुषा दृशा ।
सुरतनाथ तेऽशुल्कदासिका वरद निघ्नतो नेह किं वधः ॥
verses.translation: O Lord of love, with Your glance that steals the beauty of autumn lotus blooms, we are Your unpaid maidservants, O bestower of boons — is it not like killing us that You neglect us?

verses.sanskrit:
विषजलाप्ययाद् व्यालराक्षसाद्वर्षमारुताद् वैद्युतानलात् ।
वृषमयात्मजाद्विश्वतो भयादृषभ ते वयं रक्षिता मुहुः ॥
verses.translation: O greatest of heroes, You have always protected us from poisoned water, from the terrible serpent, from storms and lightning, from the bull demon, from the son of Maya — from all kinds of fearful situations.

verses.sanskrit:
तव कथामृतं तप्तजीवनं कविभिरीडितं कल्मषापहम् ।
श्रवणमङ्गलं श्रीमदाततं भुवि गृणन्ति ते भूरिदा जनाः ॥
verses.translation: The nectar of Your words and the descriptions of Your deeds are the life of those who suffer. Praised by sages, they destroy sins, bring auspiciousness to the ears, and broadcast divine grace. Those who spread Your glories are the most generous.
